newsitem.title: UK: UK TV show unveils Cadbury sponsorship link-up.
newsitem.headline: UK TV show unveils Cadbury sponsorship link-up.

text.p: Britain's popular commercial television soap opera, Coronation Street, has unwrapped a 10 million pound sponsorship deal with confectionery and soft drinks giant Cadbury Schweppes Plc, Cadbury said on Thursday.
The 52-week package, which allows Cadbury's name to appear at the beginning, middle and end of the show, will be seen for the first time by the show's 18 million viewers this Friday.

"This is the biggest sponsorship deal in the history of ITV (Independent Television)...We have signed a one year contract (with the show) but we're optimistic that it will go beyond that," Alan Palmer, marketing director of Cadbury told reporters at a news conference.

The launch of specially-designed 'bumper' credits -- animated to look like a street completely made of chocolate -- is timed to coincide with the introduction of a fourth weekly episode of Coronation Street, the 36-year-old soap opera, which is produced by Granada Television Ltd in Manchester.

First announced in May, Cadbury's "very significant", 10 million pound investment in the show will come partly out of its 25-30 million pound advertising budget, but includes some new cash, Palmer told Reuters.
It will continue with regular TV advertising , he said.

The agreement is part of a growing trend among UK advertisers to link up with commercial TV shows. Sponsorship allows them to promote their brand during prime viewing times, in slots uncluttered by the rivals' products, industry sources said.

"Broadcasting is changing and the relationship between broadcasters and advertisers is changing...we can't turn our back on promotions," Andrea Wonfor, joint managing director of Granada International Productions said, when asked whether viewers would be upset by Coronation Street carrying a sponsor's message.

The deal incorporates off-air promotional activities, linking the chocolate brand with the show's stars and also an on-screen promotional competition offering cash prizes. No chocolate products will be shown in the credits as this is banned by the Independent Television Commisssion, the industry watchdog.

Cadbury-Schweppes, which reported on Wednesday half-year pre-tax profits up 12 percent to 231 million pounds sterling ($362.2 million), is the fourth largest confectionery group in the world behind Nestle, Mars and Suchard.
